definition: to become or make less intense; to reduce in amount or value; (law) to put an end to
chinese: 減弱；緩和；減少；降低；（法律）廢除
example: This action would not have been sufficient to abate the odor nuisance.

definition: refrained from something by choice; chose not to vote
chinese: 戒除；避免；（投票）棄權
example: Several members abstained from voting because of a conflict of interest.

definition: difficulties; misfortune; a state of hardship
chinese: 逆境；厄運；困境
example: Adversity and prosperity reveal one's breadth of mind; joy and anger test one's self-restraint.

definition: to publicly support or recommend; a person who supports a cause; a lawyer who pleads a case
chinese: v. 提倡；擁護；主張；n. 擁護者；倡導者；辯護律師
example: More and more environmentalists advocate and use environmentally friendly unleaded petrol in cars.

definition: to make suffering or a problem less severe; to relieve
chinese: 減輕；緩和；舒緩
example: In order to alleviate employment pressures, the nation has established a series of relevant policies.

definition: the perfect example of something; the highest point of development; elevation to divine status
chinese: 典範；極致；巔峰；神化
example: As difficult as it is to imagine, the apotheosis of Mark Zuckerberg’s career, many believe, is yet to come.

definition: belonging to the nobility; distinguished in manner or bearing; haughty
chinese: 貴族的；有貴族氣派的；高傲的
example: The portrait emphasizes the subject's aristocratic bearing and formal dress.

definition: with great care and persistent effort; diligently
chinese: 勤勉地；刻苦地；專心仔細地
example: She worked assiduously to verify every citation in the report.

definition: to make an unpleasant feeling less intense; to calm; to satisfy (an appetite or desire)
chinese: 緩和；減輕；平息；滿足（慾望）
example: This medicine will assuage the pain.

definition: extremely wicked or cruel; of very poor quality
chinese: 殘暴的；兇殘的；極惡劣的；糟透的
example: He is apt to say atrocious things and to exaggerate his grievances.

definition: showing bold willingness to take risks; recklessly daring; impudent
chinese: 大膽的；無畏的；魯莽的；厚顏的
example: Only an audacious mind will be able to solve this riddle.

definition: relating to a ruler with absolute power; domineering and demanding obedience
chinese: 獨裁的；專制的；專橫的
example: an autocratic person

definition: acting independently; self-governing; operating without human control
chinese: 自主的；自治的；獨立的；自動運作的
example: The laboratory remained autonomous despite its partnership with the university.

definition: to scold or criticize angrily and at length
chinese: 嚴厲斥責；痛罵
example: If you berate me like that again, I will quit.

definition: infatuated to the point of foolishness; intoxicated
chinese: 迷戀的；痴迷的；醉醺醺的
example: He is completely besotted with her.

definition: using high-sounding but empty language; pompous
chinese: 誇大的；浮誇的；誇誇其談的
example: The dictator gave a bombastic speech.

definition: concise expression; shortness of duration
chinese: 簡潔；簡短；（時間）短暫
example: When you send a telegram, brevity is essential because you will be charged for every word.

definition: full to the point of overflowing
chinese: 充滿的；滿溢的
example: The archive is brimming with letters that illuminate the author's early career.

definition: round or bulging in shape; growing from a bulb
chinese: 球狀的；圓鼓的；（植物）有球莖的
example: The plant stores water in a bulbous stem during the dry season.

definition: a general rule or standard; an accepted body of great works; the authentic works of a writer; sacred scripture; the official storyline
chinese: 準則；標準；經典作品；（作家）真作；正典；（作品）正統設定
example: I get that this game is a spin-off, but is the story canon?

definition: annoyance or distress at failure or humiliation; to cause such distress
chinese: n. 懊惱；氣惱；v. 使懊惱
example: He often hastens physical intimacy, much to the chagrin of his dates.

definition: severe criticism or scolding; punishment
chinese: 嚴厲斥責；懲罰
example: Public chastisement only made the reluctant employee more defensive.

definition: forced; obtained by threats or force
chinese: 被迫的；受脅迫的；以脅迫取得的
example: The witness insisted that the confession had been coerced.

definition: clear, logical, and convincing; pertinent
chinese: 有說服力的；令人信服的；切題的
example: Something that’s cogent is clear and persuasive.

definition: having knowledge or awareness; aware
chinese: 意識到的；知曉的
example: They who dream by day are cognizant of many things which escape those who dream only by night.

definition: to placate; to reconcile; to win over by friendly acts
chinese: 安撫；調解；贏得（好感）
example: To conciliate is to make peace with.

definition: showing great skill; complete or perfect; to complete; to make perfect; to complete (a marriage) by sexual intercourse
chinese: adj. 技藝高超的；完美的；道地的；v. 完成；使圓滿；完婚
example: He is a consummate professional in his field.

definition: a person or thing with the same function or position as another
chinese: 對應的人或物；地位相當者
example: I tried to close the discussions at noon, but my counterpart would not stop talking.

definition: contemptibly lacking in courage; a coward
chinese: adj. 怯懦的；膽小的；n. 懦夫
example: The president is too craven to tackle this problem.

definition: the quality of believing too readily; gullibility
chinese: 輕信；易受騙
example: The scheme succeeded because it exploited the investors' credulousness.

definition: showing a critical or disrespectful attitude; insulting
chinese: 貶損的；輕蔑的；侮辱的
example: The editor removed the derogatory remark from the final article.

definition: to catch sight of; to discern from a distance
chinese: 看出；遠遠望見；發現
example: From the ridge, the hikers could descry a cabin through the fog.

definition: in low spirits from loss of hope or courage
chinese: 沮喪的；灰心的；絕望的
example: After repeated setbacks, the once-confident team became despondent.

definition: to free from a mistaken belief
chinese: 使醒悟；糾正（錯誤觀念）
example: Nothing could disabuse them of that preposterous notion.

definition: to perceive or recognize; to distinguish with difficulty
chinese: 辨別；察覺；看出；識別
example: Oleg's voice was too far away to discern what he was saying.

definition: causing unease or confusion
chinese: 令人不安的；令人困惑的
example: The sudden silence was more disconcerting than the earlier argument.

definition: to conceal one's true motives or feelings; to put on a false appearance
chinese: 掩飾；假裝；隱藏（真實感情或動機）
example: Dissemble all your griefs and discontents.

definition: revealed (secret or private information)
chinese: 洩露；透露；公開
example: The official divulged the findings only after the review was complete.

definition: the quality of being unconventional or odd; an odd habit; deviation from a circular path
chinese: 古怪；怪癖；反常行為；（數學）離心率
example: His habit of annotating menus was a harmless eccentricity.

definition: deeply involved in a conflict or difficult situation
chinese: 捲入（紛爭）的；糾纏不清的
example: embroiled in the conflict

definition: famous and respected within a particular field; outstanding
chinese: 傑出的；卓越的；顯著的
example: She is considered an eminent authority in the field of international law.

definition: a speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly
chinese: 讚詞；頌詞；讚美
example: In this context, “encomium” refers to a formal expression of praise.

definition: followed afterward or as a result (past tense of ensue)
chinese: 隨後發生；接著出現
example: A lengthy debate ensued after the committee announced its proposal.

definition: requires or involves as a necessary part or consequence (third-person form of entail)
chinese: 需要；必然包含；使成為必要
example: Restoring the bridge entails years of careful engineering work.

definition: asked earnestly or urgently (past tense of entreat)
chinese: 懇求；乞求
example: Residents entreated the council to preserve the historic market.

definition: an inscription on a tombstone; a short text commemorating a person or event
chinese: 墓誌銘；紀念短文
example: The brief epitaph captures the poet's wit and humility.

definition: mental calmness and composure, especially under stress
chinese: 沉著；鎮定；平靜
example: he accepted their problems with composure and she with equanimity

definition: to clear from blame or guilt; to free from an obligation
chinese: 證明無罪；開脫；免除（責任）
example: New laboratory evidence may exonerate the wrongly accused technician.

definition: silly and pointless; foolish in a smug way; inane
chinese: 愚蠢的；昏庸的；自鳴得意而愚蠢的
example: This is going to sound completely fatuous, but it's my honest answer.

definition: intensely enthusiastic or passionate; ardent; (literary) burning hot
chinese: 熱情的；熱烈的；激情的；酷熱的
example: The passage describes its subject as fervid, meaning characterized by intense emotion.

definition: (of style) elaborately ornate; flowery; excessively decorated; (of complexion) ruddy
chinese: （文風）華麗的；辭藻浮誇的；過分修飾的；（臉色）紅潤的
example: Her prose is full of needlessly florid, cliched descriptions, securing her career as a romance novelist.

definition: to prevent or hinder by acting in advance; to anticipate
chinese: 預先阻止；搶先；防範
example: Our aim is to forestall all those risks.

definition: in a secret, sly manner meant to avoid notice
chinese: 偷偷地；鬼鬼祟祟地
example: The student glanced furtively at the clock during the lecture.

definition: incapable of producing any useful result; pointless
chinese: 徒勞的；無效的；無用的
example: There is nothing which exacts a higher price than revenge, yet is so futile.

definition: excessively talkative, especially about trivial things
chinese: 喋喋不休的；多話的；饒舌的
example: Garrulous as he may have been, that old philosopher made some very poignant arguments about economics and society.

definition: extravagantly bright or showy; tastelessly ornate
chinese: 俗麗的；花俏的；炫耀的
example: Don't you think that necklace is a bit gaudy?

definition: in a careful or cautious manner; cautious
chinese: adv. 小心翼翼地；謹慎地；adj. 小心翼翼的
example: The conservator gingerly lifted the fragile manuscript from its case.

definition: to provoke or urge into action; to spur; a stimulus; a pointed stick for driving cattle
chinese: v. 刺激；驅使；激勵；n. 刺激物；刺棒
example: The coach's motivational speech was a goad for the team's determination.

definition: to overcharge or swindle; to scoop out; a chisel with a curved blade; a deep groove
chinese: v. 敲竹槓；剝削；挖出；n. 圓鑿；鑿痕
example: Reputable vendors do not gouge customers during an emergency.

definition: fond of company; sociable; (of animals) living in groups
chinese: 愛交際的；合群的；（動物）群居的
example: Often we think that great leaders are those who are gregarious, always in the middle of a large group of people; yet, as Mahatma Gandhi and many others have shown us, leaders can often be introverted.

definition: passed on genetically; inherited by succession; handed down from ancestors
chinese: 遺傳的；世襲的；祖傳的
example: Researchers found that the disorder was hereditary rather than contagious.

definition: a break or interruption in continuity; a gap
chinese: 中斷；暫停；空隙
example: The journal returned after a two-year publication hiatus.

definition: exaggerated dramatic behavior meant to draw attention; theatrical performances
chinese: 誇張做作的舉止；裝腔作勢；戲劇表演
example: Her calm rebuttal ended the debate without unnecessary histrionics.

definition: giving strong encouragement; exhorting
chinese: 勸誡的；激勵的；鼓勵的
example: Her hortatory speech encouraged the volunteers to continue their work.

definition: deliberate exaggeration used for emphasis
chinese: 誇飾；誇張法；誇大其詞
example: I could eat a horse, and that's not hyperbole.

definition: about to happen; impending
chinese: 即將發生的；迫近的
example: The dark clouds and swirling wind indicated that a storm was imminent.

definition: to call into question; to attack as false or wrong
chinese: 質疑；抨擊；責難（動機或誠信）
example: The father does not impugn her ability to be a good mother.

definition: in a keenly perceptive and direct way
chinese: 敏銳地；一針見血地；犀利地
example: The reviewer incisively identified the argument's central weakness.

definition: not readily noticed; not attracting attention
chinese: 不顯眼的；不引人注意的
example: The sensor is small enough to remain inconspicuous on the wall.

definition: originating naturally in a region; native; of the original inhabitants; inherent
chinese: 本土的；原生的；原住民的；固有的
example: The area was inhabited for thousands of years by succeeding cultures of indigenous peoples.

definition: anger provoked by something unjust or wrong
chinese: 憤慨；義憤
example: The unfair accusation provoked widespread indignation among the researchers.

definition: lacking skill or competence; clumsy; inappropriate; absurd
chinese: 無能的；笨拙的；不得當的；荒謬的
example: This cloth has the special ability to be invisible to the stupid and the inept.

definition: evil reputation; the state of being notorious; a shameful act
chinese: 惡名；聲名狼藉；醜行
example: The failed expedition passed into infamy because its leaders ignored repeated warnings.

definition: gross injustice; immoral behavior; a wicked act
chinese: 極不公正；邪惡；罪行
example: We have taken part in the iniquity that will happen.

definition: unaware (of); lacking sensation; unconscious; indifferent; too slight to be perceived
chinese: 未察覺的；無知覺的；不省人事的；麻木的；難以察覺的
example: Lucy lay senseless on the ground, insensible of the wonderful deliverance which she had experienced.

definition: unwilling to change one's views or to compromise; uncompromising
chinese: 不妥協的；固執的；不讓步的
example: He is a stubborn and intransigent demagogue.

definition: in a cheerful, friendly, good-humored way
chinese: 快活地；愉快地
example: The host jovially welcomed every guest at the door.

definition: to tear or deeply cut (flesh or skin); to wound the feelings of; to criticize harshly
chinese: 撕裂；割傷；使痛苦；嚴厲抨擊
example: If you don't wear protective clothing, the sharp leaves will lacerate your skin.

definition: freedom; the right to act as one chooses; presumptuous or overly familiar behavior
chinese: 自由；自主權；冒昧；放肆
example: The constitution protects individual liberty while permitting reasonable regulation.

definition: sexually unrestrained; lacking moral restraint; disregarding rules
chinese: 放蕩的；淫亂的；放肆的；不守規範的
example: He was converted from his licentious living.

definition: very talkative; garrulous
chinese: 多話的；健談的；喋喋不休的
example: Her loquacious new beau was there, talking everyone's heads off.

definition: clarity of expression; clearness of thought; sanity; transparency
chinese: 清晰；明晰；神智清醒；清澈
example: The essay's lucidity makes a difficult theory accessible.

definition: so absurd as to be laughable; ridiculous
chinese: 荒謬的；可笑的；荒唐的
example: The storylines in this series have got more and more ludicrous.

definition: noble and generous in spirit, esp. toward a rival or offender
chinese: 寬宏大量的；有雅量的；慷慨的
example: In a serious struggle there is no worse cruelty than to be magnanimous at an inopportune time.

definition: expressing a threat; menacing; ominous
chinese: 威脅的；恐嚇的；有凶兆的
example: The letter's minatory language warned of severe consequences.

definition: to calm or soothe the anger of; to appease; to lessen in intensity
chinese: 安撫；平息（怒氣）；緩和
example: You won’t mollify him with that explanation.

definition: a complicated or confusing situation; a swamp or bog
chinese: 困境；亂局；泥淖；沼澤
example: The simple dispute became a legal morass after several appeals.

definition: to remove (a need or difficulty); to make unnecessary; to prevent
chinese: 排除；消除；使不必要；預防
example: These days, a smart phone with a good data plan can obviate the need for a land line.

definition: a public spectacle with elaborate costumes, often depicting history; an impressive display; a beauty contest; empty or showy display
chinese: 盛大遊行；露天歷史劇；壯觀場面；選美比賽；虛飾
example: Do you know what the name of last year's beauty pageant winner is?

definition: relating to or consisting of money
chinese: 金錢的；金錢上的；財務的
example: I'm suffering from pecuniary embarrassment.

definition: full of danger or risk; hazardous; precarious
chinese: 危險的；冒險的；岌岌可危的
example: A coward is someone who, in a perilous emergency, thinks with his legs.

definition: childishly sulky or bad-tempered; easily irritated
chinese: 任性易怒的；愛發脾氣的；耍性子的
example: Stop acting like a petulant child every time you don't get your way.

definition: to prevent from happening; to make impossible in advance; to rule out
chinese: 排除；阻止；使不可能；預先防止
example: That, of course, would effectively preclude the underlying tombs ever being investigated archaeologically.

definition: evasive speech or action; deliberate deviation from the truth; lying
chinese: 支吾其詞；推諉；搪塞；說謊
example: Repeated prevarication damaged the spokesperson's credibility.

definition: announced or declared officially (past of proclaim); openly declared or acknowledged
chinese: v. 宣告；宣布；正式宣稱；adj. 公開宣稱的；公認的
example: The panel proclaimed the experiment a success after reviewing the data.

definition: producing much work or many results; plentiful; producing many offspring
chinese: 多產的；豐富的；繁殖力強的；大量的
example: a prolific writer

definition: likely to suffer or do something; inclined to; lying face downward
chinese: 易於……的；有……傾向的；俯臥的；趴著的
example: Coastal roads are prone to flooding during severe storms.

definition: a natural inclination or tendency
chinese: 傾向；癖好；習性
example: From a very young age, he showed his propensity for studying.

definition: prolonging; drawing out in time (present participle of protract)
chinese: 拖延；延長；使拖長
example: Further procedural objections were merely protracting the negotiations.

definition: complaining in a whining or petulant way; peevish
chinese: 愛抱怨的；發牢騷的；易怒的
example: She spoke in a querulous voice.

definition: trivial complaints or objections; evasive arguments
chinese: 小異議；吹毛求疵的批評；遁詞
example: Minor quibbles should not obscure the proposal's broad merits.

definition: stubbornly resistant to authority or control; (of a disease) not responsive to treatment; (of a material) heat-resistant
chinese: 倔強的；難駕馭的；（疾病）難治的；耐高溫的；難熔的
example: Owing to the refractory nature of alumina it is with difficulty that it can be diffused in alkaline silicates, borates, or lead silicates.

definition: a quick, sharp, or witty reply; a retort; (law) a defendant's answer to a plaintiff's reply
chinese: 機敏的回答；反駁；（法律）被告第二次答辯
example: Her concise rejoinder exposed the weakness of the criticism.

definition: able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions; (of a material) springing back into shape
chinese: 有韌性的；能迅速復原的；有彈性的
example: The resilient ecosystem recovered quickly after the drought.

definition: (of a sound) to be repeated as an echo; to have continuing and serious effects
chinese: 迴盪；迴響；產生持續影響
example: The loud sounds of sawing, drilling and scraping reverberate around the room.

definition: to soak thoroughly; to fill completely; to cause to reach saturation; to supply a market beyond demand
chinese: 浸透；使充滿；使飽和；（市場）飽和
example: Kaleidoscopic prints saturate my blank mind, creating vital memories and burning thoughts.

definition: able to perceive or feel things; conscious
chinese: 有知覺的；有意識的；能感受的
example: The novel asks whether an artificial intelligence could become sentient.

definition: tending to induce sleep; tediously boring; a drug or thing that induces sleep
chinese: adj. 催眠的；令人昏昏欲睡的；n. 安眠藥；催眠物
example: The book I bought yesterday is a real soporific.

definition: not genuine; fake; based on false reasoning
chinese: 虛假的；偽造的；謬誤的；似是而非的
example: The argument that the platform exists only to promote written language seems spurious.

definition: spoke haltingly, with involuntary pauses and repetitions (past tense of stammer)
chinese: 結巴地說；口吃
example: Surprised by the accusation, he stammered an incomplete reply.

definition: the quality of showing little emotion; impassiveness
chinese: 冷漠；無動於衷；遲鈍
example: The guard's stolidity concealed considerable anxiety.

definition: thwarted; blocked
chinese: 受阻的；被妨礙的
example: The investigation was stymied by incomplete and contradictory records.

definition: diminished or abated (past tense of subside)
chinese: 減弱；平息；消退
example: The crowd resumed its discussion after the noise subsided.

definition: reserved and uncommunicative in speech
chinese: 沉默寡言的；不愛說話的
example: Jason was a taciturn individual, so it was always a real surprise when he said anything.

definition: a long, angry speech of criticism or accusation
chinese: 長篇激烈的抨擊；激烈的長篇演說
example: In terms of political change, a tirade oftentimes does little more than make the person speaking red in the face.

definition: a large, heavy, scholarly book
chinese: 厚重的大書；學術鉅著
example: The historian's new tome examines three centuries of regional trade.

definition: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy; apathy; dormancy
chinese: 遲鈍；麻木；懶散；冷漠；蟄伏
example: In this context, “torpor” refers to a state of motor and mental inactivity with a partial suspension of sensibility.

definition: easy to deal with or control; docile; manageable
chinese: 易處理的；易駕馭的；溫順的
example: It may not be easy, but this problem is tractable.

definition: continuing without any reduction in intensity
chinese: 未減弱的；持續強烈的
example: Public interest in the discovery continued unabated for months.

definition: unable to be challenged or questioned; impossible to attack or defeat
chinese: 無可辯駁的；無可置疑的；攻不破的
example: Being convinced of your own unassailable rationality is like being convinced of the solidity of a mirage.

definition: not pretentious or arrogant; modest
chinese: 謙遜的；不張揚的；不擺架子的
example: The unassuming scientist rarely mentioned her many awards.

definition: not intimidated or discouraged by difficulty; resolute
chinese: 無畏的；不屈不撓的；勇敢堅定的
example: Undaunted by the initial rejection, the team revised its proposal.

definition: left or emptied (a place); gave up (a position); annulled (a ruling)
chinese: 空出；騰出；離開；（法律）撤銷
example: The tenants vacated the building before repairs began.

definition: wavered indecisively between options; swayed back and forth
chinese: 猶豫不決；搖擺不定
example: The committee vacillated between caution and rapid reform.

definition: deeply respected; revered
chinese: 受敬重的；受崇敬的
example: The venerated scholar continued teaching well into retirement.

definition: through the experiences of another person; secondhand; in place of another
chinese: 間接地；感同身受地；代替地
example: Readers experience the explorer's discoveries vicariously through her journals.

definition: competing eagerly with others for something
chinese: 競爭；爭奪
example: Several laboratories are vying to reproduce the surprising result.

definition: a confused mass; turmoil; to roll or wallow; to be deeply involved
chinese: n. 混亂；雜亂的一團；v. 翻滾；沉溺
example: Without a word, he had disappeared into the welter of the noonday crowd.

definition: playfully quaint or fanciful; odd; acting on whim; capricious
chinese: 古怪的；異想天開的；奇特有趣的；反覆無常的
example: She shaped the cake into a whimsical design.
